bugs.explanation: `calc()` requires whitespace around `+` and `-` operators. `calc(100%-240px)` is invalid CSS and the browser will ignore the `width` rule entirely. Write `calc(100% - 240px)` with spaces on both sides of the minus sign.

`position: sticky` requires at least one threshold property (`top`, `bottom`, `left`, or `right`) to define where the element sticks. Without `top: 0`, the element behaves like `position: relative` and never sticks. Add `top: 0;` after the `position` declaration.

title: CSS Variable Fallback Wrong Type

bugs.explanation: The fallback value `red` is a color, but `width` expects a length. If `--box-width` is undefined, the browser gets `width: red` which is invalid and the property is ignored. Provide a sensible length fallback: `var(--box-width, 200px)`.

title: pointer-events none Blocks Child Clicks
overflow hidden Clips Absolute Child

bugs.explanation: `overflow: hidden` clips all content that extends outside the element's box — including `position: absolute` children. The `.badge` positioned at `top: -10px; right: -10px` will be cropped. If you need the badge to overflow, remove `overflow: hidden` or move the badge outside the `.card` element.

`flex` with two values sets `flex-grow` and `flex-shrink`, but the `flex-basis` defaults to `0` in this two-value syntax (not `auto`). `flex: 1 0` means the item can grow but not shrink, with a basis of `0px` — potentially collapsing to nothing. Use three values explicitly: `flex: 1 0 auto` to clarify intent.

A `<div>` with `onclick` and `tabindex` is not semantically a button. Screen readers announce it as a generic region, not a button. Users expect `Enter` and `Space` to activate buttons — a `<div>` doesn't handle these by default. Replace `<div>` with `<button>` and remove the `onclick` in favour of an event listener or `type="button"`.

title: aria-label on Element With Visible Text

bugs.explanation: When a button already has clear visible text ('Submit'), adding `aria-label` overrides that text for screen readers and creates a mismatch — users may hear 'Submit the form' while sighted users see 'Submit'. Remove redundant `aria-label` from elements that already have descriptive visible text. Use `aria-label` only when there is no visible label.

Without `initial-scale=1`, some browsers (especially iOS Safari) may zoom in or out by default, causing the layout to appear at an unexpected scale. Always include both `width=device-width` and `initial-scale=1` in the viewport meta tag.

title: tabindex Positive Value Breaks Tab Order
code: Home About Contact

bugs.explanation: Positive `tabindex` values create a separate tab order that runs before the natural DOM order, causing confusing navigation for keyboard users. Remove all positive tabindex values — links and buttons are already focusable by default and follow the DOM order naturally. Use `tabindex="0"` only when adding a non-focusable element to the tab order, and `tabindex="-1"` to remove an element from the tab order programmatically.

title: srcset Using px Instead of w Descriptor

bugs.explanation: `srcset` width descriptors use `w` (not `px`) to specify the intrinsic width of each image source in pixels. Using `px` is invalid — the browser will ignore the `srcset` and fall back to `src`. Replace `400px` with `400w` and `800px` with `800w`.

title: transition on all Properties

bugs.explanation: `transition: all` animates every CSS property that changes — including ones you didn't intend like `width`, `height`, or `color` during dynamic updates. This triggers unnecessary style recalculations and repaints, hurting performance. Specify only the properties you intend to animate: `transition: transform 0.3s ease`.

`will-change: all` tells the browser to prepare a compositor layer for every possible property, consuming significant memory and defeating the purpose of the hint. Specify only the property you're actually animating: `will-change: transform`. And prefer removing `will-change` after the animation completes to free resources.

The `lang` attribute on `<html>` tells browsers and screen readers what language the page is in. Without it, screen readers may use the wrong language voice/pronunciation, search engines may rank the page incorrectly for localised queries, and spell-checkers can behave unexpectedly. Always specify `lang` on the root element.

Removing `outline` on `:focus` destroys the visible keyboard focus indicator. Keyboard-only users and people with motor disabilities lose all ability to tell which element is focused. Either keep the default outline, or replace it with a custom visible style: `outline: 2px solid #0066cc;` or use `outline-offset`.

A fixed `height` prevents the element from growing when content exceeds it. Combined with `overflow: hidden`, longer content is silently clipped and invisible. Use `min-height` instead to set a floor while allowing the dialog to expand with its content.

A `display: grid` container without `grid-template-columns` creates a single-column grid — all items stack vertically. To create a multi-column layout, specify the columns: `grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr)` for three equal columns, or `auto-fill`/`auto-fit` with `minmax()` for responsive behaviour.

title: img Without width and height Causes Layout Shift
code: Shop our latest deals.

bugs.explanation: Without explicit `width` and `height` attributes, the browser doesn't know the image's aspect ratio until it downloads. This causes Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) — text and elements below the image jump down once the image loads. Set `width` and `height` matching the image's intrinsic size so the browser reserves the correct space.

title: Clean Responsive Image (No Bugs)
font-size in px Ignores User Preferences

bugs.explanation: Setting `font-size` in `px` on `<html>` overrides the user's browser font-size preference (typically settable in browser settings for accessibility). Users who need larger text to read comfortably will not benefit from their setting. Use `font-size: 100%` (or `1rem`-based units throughout) to respect the browser default, which is controlled by the user.
